core.title: Bind emitting source to its tracking-plan item with a resolving telemetry header
core.given: In a telemetry-adopting repository, implementation (non-test) source emits telemetry or carries a telemetry binding header.
core.when: The source is written, edited or checked, or the tracking plan renames or removes an item.
core.then: Each telemetry item the file emits is declared by name in a telemetry binding header (the profile's binding syntax), and every binding header names a concrete telemetry URN (the profile's URN shape) matching the identity field of a tracking-plan item in the telemetry registry (the profile's registry root, entry location, entry serialization and entry identity field).
prefer: A binding header placed directly above the emitting code, in the profile's binding syntax.
One binding header per emitted item.
Update binding headers in the same change when the tracking plan renames an item.
avoid: Emitting telemetry with no binding header.
Non-concrete URNs (missing parts, wildcards, placeholders), measured against the profile's telemetry URN shape.
URNs naming no tracking-plan item, including stale ones after a rename.
Writing the binding in anything other than the profile's header syntax (other comment forms, markup attributes) or inside a string literal; such text is not a header.
Naming an item the file does not emit just to make it resolve.
unless: Capability not adopted (no telemetry registry root and no telemetry declaration in any acceptance artifact anywhere): the rule emits nothing, whichever profiles run.
Test files (unit, acceptance and e2e test roles): they legitimately name telemetry items while asserting them.
core.why: The binding header is the source-to-telemetry traceability edge; like Tested-By, a checkable promise: the URN is well-formed and the tracking-plan registry holds it.
evidence: The telemetry check reports no grammar finding (a non-concrete URN) for any binding header in implementation source.
The telemetry check reports no resolution finding: every binding-header URN matches the identity field of a tracking-plan item in the registry.
Review confirms that every implementation (non-test) file that emits telemetry carries a binding header naming each item it emits, and only the items it emits.
verification: The check parses only the profile's telemetry binding header syntax in implementation (non-test) source; an occurrence inside a string literal is not a header, and constructs outside the binding syntax (other comment forms, markup attributes) are not parsed.

Two distinct failures are reported: grammar (the value is not a concrete telemetry URN per the profile's shape) and resolution (grammatical but no tracking-plan item in the registry carries that id in its identity field).
The header binds the file to the concrete item it emits, and the check scans all existing headers, not only those changed in the current diff.
Test files are excluded from the scan (tests are implementation's mirror, not implementation: they legitimately name items while asserting them).
Inert until adopted: with no telemetry registry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration anywhere, the check emits nothing regardless of which profiles run.

The declaration half of the obligation (implementation source that emits telemetry names it in a header) has no mechanical detector in this rule's check; it is established by review/LLM judgment of emission.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: Implementation source in an adopting repository carries a telemetry binding header whose value is not a concrete telemetry URN in the profile's shape.
An existing, unchanged binding header names a grammatical URN that has no tracking-plan item in the registry.
A tracking-plan item is renamed or removed while source binding headers still reference the old URN.
Implementation source in an adopting repository emits a telemetry item but has no binding header naming it.
The repository has no telemetry registry root but has an acceptance telemetry declaration, and a source binding header is non-concrete, unresolved, or missing for emitted telemetry.
doesNotFire: The repository has no telemetry registry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration anywhere (capability not adopted), whatever profiles run.
The binding-header text appears in, or telemetry is named by, a test file (telemetry tests legitimately name items while asserting them).
The binding-header text appears inside a string literal.
The reference is written in a form outside the profile's binding syntax (e.g. another comment form or a markup attribute), which the check does not parse.
Implementation source that emits no telemetry and carries no binding header.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root tree of the telemetry tracking-plan registry; its existence is adoption signal 1 and the registry against which header URNs resolve.

The stack's concrete construct for one tracking-plan registry entry: how the entry is serialized.
The identity field of a telemetry tracking-plan registry entry: the identifier field whose value is the telemetry URN a source header must match for resolution.

profileRequirements.meaning: URN shape of one telemetry tracking-plan item; concreteness of a header value is judged against this shape.
The syntax by which implementation source binds itself to a telemetry item (the binding header the check parses).

neutralityNotes: All profile references use existing vocabulary v3 keys: the telemetry URN shape and binding-header syntax come from the parametric urn keys (urn.telemetry, urn.binding.telemetry), the registry root from roots.telemetry, and the tracking-plan entry's location, serialization and identity field from layout.locations#telemetry_item (location pattern only), idiom.telemetry#registry_entry (JSON serialization) and urn.grammar#telemetry_item_identity_field (identity-field grammar), each key restricted to the aspect its doc covers. The Bun activation fact type path_glob is not in the neutral fact vocabulary and was normalized to file_kind (value: telemetry registry root exists). The acceptance-declaration adoption signal has no concrete syntax in bun.json, so it stays role-level (needs_new_observer in any realization). Validator and term ids (bun_telemetry_code, telemetry_reference, tracking_plan_item) remain bunOnly; the core describes the check generically. Severity 2 and the strict disposition (fail on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline) are per-rule and live in core:verification, not in the profile. The declaration half of the obligation (emitting source names what it emits) has no mechanical emission observer, so it stays review/LLM-judged in every realization.
